# What the data-dict export loses: National Survey of Family Growth

The YAML files here follow data-dict spec 0.1.0. They describe the common data format, so they validate against its parquet files. The records in `metadata/` remain canonical. This table counts what the export drops or flattens into text.

| | `2022-2023` | `2017-2019` |
|---|---|---|
| variables exported | 55 | 49 |
| variables whose numeric code labels went to `details` (no labeled numeric codes) | 45 | 39 |
| missing or unresolved codes, typed only in the `__code` column's labels | 48 | 34 |
| variables with several wordings, flattened into `details` | 4 | 0 |
| availability entries (wave by form, with n), summarized as one line of text | 55 | 49 |
| corrections applied; only the corrected text is exported | 1 | 0 |
| field origins (publisher, data file, rule, hand, model) not exported | 348 | 356 |
| links between releases, not exported | 18 | 18 |
| derived properties (scale signatures), not exported | 2 | 2 |
| release id not expressible as data-dict `version` (needs semver or a date) | 1 | 1 |
